key_reasoning.reason: Three alembic migrations (enum add, data migration, singleton index), Settings model (check_ms_teams_singleton), two routers (project_settings.py, user_settings.py), settings_request_validator.py (new validate_ms_teams_request), and codemie_tools/base/models.py (CredentialTypes.MS_TEAMS) — 6+ components spanning DB-Persistence, Service, and API layers, plus a new invariant (application read-then-write check backed by a DB partial unique index).

Irreversible data migration: assistant_project_mapping rows are deduped/merged into settings.credential_values by project_name with no filter on the mapping table's `feature` column, then the source table, its FK, unique constraint, and index are dropped. If any assistant_project_mapping rows belonged to a feature other than ms_teams, that data is silently folded into MS_TEAMS credentials with no way to recover it — downgrade() reconstructs the table but not the original per-row feature/created_at/updated_by values. Combined with the new partial-unique-index concurrency guard, this has no exact precedent in the codebase.

diffstat reports 33 files changed (mapped to XXL per the 16+ threshold). Note: the bulk of that count is docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-08-27-teams-integ-1-foundation/* artifacts from a prior, already-landed task bundled into the same diff, not new work for this migration story; the code-relevant footprint is 14 files (.gitignore, 5 app modules, 3 new alembic revisions, 5 test files).

DB-Persistence (3 alembic revisions, settings table schema/index changes), Service (settings_request_validator.validate_ms_teams_request, Settings.check_ms_teams_singleton), and API (project_settings.py, user_settings.py routing) — a schema-change/migration spanning three layers.
